name: Uniform Relative Nerve for Prescribed Coefficients
statement: Under protected exact reduction with at most two terminal rows per local system, the fiber of prescribed-row restriction at log parameter $x$ is homotopy equivalent to the finite complex $\mathcal N_x$ whose nonempty faces $F$ satisfy $x\in P_F$. The restriction image is the union of the singleton domains. A finite rational central hyperplane arrangement has constant labeled complex, and hence constant fiber homotopy type, on every relatively open sign cell, including lower-dimensional cells.
proof: The parameter-preserving reduction identifies each fiber with a union of finitely many open convex sets indexed by determinant selections. Their nonempty intersections are exactly the domains $P_F$, so the open good-cover nerve theorem gives the fiber equivalence. The finitely many rational dual forms defining all $P_F$ have constant strict-sign truth values on each sign cell, making the entire labeled nerve constant there.
comments: The theorem asserts fiber homotopy types, not local triviality or homeomorphism of fibers. The face domains retain more information than a list of Betti numbers.
